title: Without the DS filter, IED− mice show a slow sink building up before the DS
plain: With no band filter, the sink 10–30 ms before the DS peak is already 24 to 95% of the peak in IED− mice and under 26% in every control; the 5–100 Hz filter takes this slow lead-in away.
how: Same events, same DS1/DS2/DS3 labels as the Halo set; only the filter on the waveform changes (zero-phase Butterworth, order 3, 60 Hz notch always, read with 2 s of margin). No filter (notch only). Every event. Per event: the sink trace (mean of the two main-sink rows) from 30 to 10 ms before the peak, divided by its value at the peak. Per recording: mean. Contrast: IED− against control.
ylabel:
Sink 30–10 ms before the peak
(share of the peak, mean)
why: Every IED− value above every control (P = 0.012). Under the DS filter P = 0.32; with 1–100 Hz P = 0.042. So it lives below 5 Hz: a slow sink that starts before the DS.
against: Not on the 1–300 Hz copy (P = 0.16), which also keeps the slow part; m7 (0.96) and m1 (0.89) carry it. IED+ mice look like controls. A slow drift unrelated to the DS would do the same; the before/after battery tests that directly.
test: The before/after battery's 1–4 Hz power before the DS in the same mice; a planned test in new IED− mice.

title: Without the DS filter, IED− mice's sinks vary more from event to event
plain: With no band filter, the size of the sink (summed over ±10 ms) varies more from one event to the next in every IED− mouse than in any control.
how: Same events, same DS1/DS2/DS3 labels as the Halo set; only the filter on the waveform changes (zero-phase Butterworth, order 3, 60 Hz notch always, read with 2 s of margin). No filter. Every event. Per event: the sink at the two main-sink rows summed from −10 to +10 ms. Per recording: CV over events (no units). Contrast: IED− against control.
ylabel:
Sink size, event to event
(CV over events, no filter)
why: IED− 0.63 to 1.26, controls 0.39 to 0.56: no overlap (P = 0.006). Under the DS filter P = 0.16; low knockout against control P = 0.017.
against: m3 (IED+, 0.92) is as variable as IED− mice. The slow part the filter removes may be drift that adds to some events and not others.
test: CV of the sink after removing the 1 s around each event's baseline, unfiltered; planned.

title: No longer under 0.05 in run 5. With a narrow 10–40 Hz filter, IED− mice's source duration varies more
plain: Kept to 10–40 Hz, the duration of the source between the blades varies more from event to event in every IED− mouse than in any control.
how: Same events, same DS1/DS2/DS3 labels as the Halo set; only the filter on the waveform changes (zero-phase Butterworth, order 3, 60 Hz notch always, read with 2 s of margin). 10–40 Hz. Every event. Per event: the source trace and its full width at half its peak (ms). Per recording: CV over events. Contrast: IED− against control.
ylabel:
Source duration, event to event
(CV over events, 10–40 Hz)
why: IED− against control P = 0.16 (run 4: no overlap, P = 0.006). 5–50 Hz P = 0.32; DS filter P = 0.79.
against: The difference was small to begin with (0.26 against 0.25 at the edges). A narrow filter rings, and ringing makes widths depend on the filter as much as on the event.
test: The same at 5–50 Hz with more mice.

title: Keeping 1–5 Hz, the net source between the blades falls more clearly with knockout
plain: The net-source lead (main lead 1, sinks left out) is stronger when the filter keeps the slow part (1–100 Hz) than under the DS filter.
how: Same events, same DS1/DS2/DS3 labels as the Halo set; only the filter on the waveform changes (zero-phase Butterworth, order 3, 60 Hz notch always, read with 2 s of margin). 1–100 Hz. Every event. Per event: mean CSD over the rows between the two blades' sinks (sink rows left out), over the sink at the main-sink rows. Per recording: mean. Contrast: rank correlation with % knockout within PTEN.
ylabel:
Net source between the blades
(sinks left out; over the sink, mean, 1–100 Hz)
why: Within PTEN rho −0.85 (P = 0.006; run 4 P = 0.014). No filter P = 0.025, 1–300 Hz P = 0.011, 10–40 Hz P = 0.037, DS filter P = 0.059.
against: Gone at 5–50 Hz (P = 0.71). m8 (1.22) and m33 (0.96), the two lowest-knockout mice, carry the correlation.

title: No longer under 0.05 in run 5. Keeping 1–5 Hz and fast activity, DS2 in IED+ mice has almost no sink before the peak
plain: Filtered 1–300 Hz, the sink 10–30 ms before a DS2 peak is about 0 to 6% of the peak in IED+ mice and 2 to 12% in controls.
how: Same events, same DS1/DS2/DS3 labels as the Halo set; only the filter on the waveform changes (zero-phase Butterworth, order 3, 60 Hz notch always, read with 2 s of margin). 1–300 Hz. DS2 events of each recording's winning classifier. Per event: the sink trace (main-sink rows) from 30 to 10 ms before the peak, divided by its value at the peak. Per recording: median. Contrast: IED+ against control.
ylabel:
Sink 30–10 ms before a DS2 peak
(share of the peak, median, 1–300 Hz)
why: IED+ against control P = 0.13 (run 4 P = 0.010). IED+ against IED− P = 0.016 still. 1–100 Hz P = 0.43; DS filter P = 0.43.
against: Not without any filter (P = 0.33). m59 (0.03) sits with IED+.
test: The before/after battery's slow power before DS2; planned test in new mice.
